citations.claim: light body gained velocity (+x,+y) from initially zero at step 0
light body vy component showing large kick
heavy body kick is much smaller in magnitude and does not balance light body momentum (m0*v0 + m1*v1 != 0)
heavy body vy component, m1*vy1 = -0.0512 vs m0*vy0 = +0.0569 leaving net +0.00569 momentum

counterfactual.change: changed heavy body mass 17.521047089796522 -> 1 (equal masses); same dt, G, positions, steps=1. Equal masses restores equal-and-opposite kicks so momentum stays conserved.

explanation: Both bodies start at rest (zero total momentum). After one step the light (m=1) body gets v~(0.00775,0.05691) while the heavy (m=17.52) body gets v~(-0.000398,-0.00292). Momenta are m0*v0=(0.00775,0.05691) vs m1*v1=(-0.00698,-0.05122), leaving net (0.00077,0.00569) — a momentum change of 0.00574 over allowed 0.00111. Speed ratio |v0|/|v1|=19.47 instead of mass-inverse 17.52, so pairwise kicks are not equal-and-opposite. Equal-mass counterfactual removes the failure, pointing to mass-ratio-dependent force asymmetry (e.g. sequential in-place update or per-body force scaling that breaks Newton's third law) rather than generic integrator error.
vision_note: Two bodies start vertically separated, with the larger body above the smaller body. At step 1 both bodies remain in essentially the same positions with no perceptible motion.
